title: Graceful edge failback: inflight request preservation, KV cache safeguard, and telemetry attenuation
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Motivation: During a regional transient we observed hard failovers that dropped in-flight requests and aggressively purged KV cache entries, causing downstream quality regressions and noisy spike metrics that triggered cascading mitigations (see Linear ENG-4281). This change implements a coordinated edge failback flow that preserves inflight requests when a region is brought back online, introduces a conservative KV cache safeguard that prevents mass evictions during topological changes, and adds a telemetry attenuation layer to prevent metric storms from driving oscillatory SLO enforcement.

What this PR does (high level):
- Inflight preservation: adds a short-lived inflight drain window on the returning region that queues or hedges requests (HEDGE) until KV warming completes or a timeout elapses. This prevents request loss and reduces cold-cache penalties.
- KV safeguard: introduces a two-phase eviction veto for KV cache during topology transitions. Evictions are batched and prioritized by inferred hotness; bulk purge routes are disabled for 60s post-failback.
- Telemetry attenuator: a sliding dampener on service-level metrics (latency/error-rate) that applies a conservative smoothing policy for the first 2 minutes after a region flip. This avoids immediate SLO-driven shedding decisions based on transient spikes.
- Safe defaults and knobs: all features disabled by default on release branch; enabled via runtime flags and remote config. Provides per-tenant overrides and an experimental opt-in for Dedicated customers.

Why this approach: The root cause in PROD was an interplay between immediate KV purges, aggressive circuit reopens, and SLO enforcers that saw a short spike as a sustained degradation. Preserving inflight work while slowly bringing state back to stable reduces tail latency and avoids unnecessary tenant quarantines.

Compatibility and rollout:
- Backwards compatible with older routing clients; behavior gated behind remote flags.
- Phased rollout plan: canary in one region (us-west-2) -> limited tenant cohort -> full ramp.
- Includes health probes and telemetry markers to track warmup and attenuation windows.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation: runtime + routing + telemetry glue
- [x] Unit tests for drain windows, KV veto logic, attenuator smoothing function
- [x] Integration tests simulating regional flip and warmup
- [x] Docs: operational runbook and console flag UI copy
- [x] Observability: histograms and event markers for warmup/attenuation windows

Related: Linear ENG-4281, ENG-4410; Support ticket SUP-1107 referenced for customer incident.
